summary: In Arkansas, new construction and work on a building's nonmechanical components (walls, roofs, wiring, plumbing) is not taxed to the customer, but installing mechanical or electrical equipment, appliances or flooring in an existing building is taxable.

conditions.when: New construction or a substantially modified building, including first-time installation of equipment and flooring there
Work on nonmechanical, passive components of an existing building (walls, roofs, doors, windows, wiring, pipes, ductwork)
Installing mechanical or electrical equipment, appliances, HVAC units or flooring in an existing building

citations.title: 26 CAR §30-1003(a)(1)(B)
citations.quote: All contractors are deemed to be consumers or users of all tangible personal property including materials, supplies, and equipment used or consumed by them in performing any contract, and the sales of all such property to contractors are taxable sales.

citations.title: 26 CAR §30-1003(b)(1)(B)
citations.quote: This means, generally, that services performed on nonmechanical components or fixtures within or on a building or other improvement to real estate are not taxable;

citations.title: 26 CAR §30-1003(b)(2)(A)
citations.quote: First-time installation of mechanical or electrical equipment into a newly constructed or substantially modified building or other improvement to real estate is not a taxable service.

citations.title: 26 CAR §30-1003(b)(2)(C)
citations.quote: The initial installation of mechanical or electrical equipment into an existing building is taxable.

citations.title: 26 CAR §30-1003(b)(3)(B)
citations.quote: The initial installation of carpet or other flooring in an existing building is taxable.

notes: A kitchen remodel in an existing building mixes the two: installing cabinets and plumbing is not taxable, installing appliances and flooring is; nontaxable charges must be separately stated or the whole charge is taxable (26 CAR §30-519(d)(4)). The contractor pays tax on materials for nontaxable work. The Code of Arkansas Rules is the official text from 2025-01-01, so the rule starts there; the same provisions were in the earlier Gross Receipts Tax Rules (GR series) but those versions were not read. Arkansas city and county sales taxes apply to the same sales as the state tax for this code, so this rule covers the state and local parts.

summary: In Arkansas, repairing a building's nonmechanical components (roofs, walls, plumbing pipes, wiring) is not taxed to the customer, but repairing or replacing mechanical or electrical equipment, appliances, flooring or carpet is taxable.

conditions.when: Repair or replacement of nonmechanical components (roofs, walls, doors, windows, pipes, wiring, ductwork, painting)
Repair or replacement of mechanical or electrical equipment, appliances, HVAC units, elevators, flooring or carpet

citations.title: 26 CAR §30-1003(a)(1)(B)

citations.quote: This means, generally, that services performed on nonmechanical components or fixtures within or on a building or other improvement to real estate are not taxable;

citations.title: 26 CAR §30-1003(c)(3)(A)
citations.quote: The initial installation, alteration, addition, cleaning, refinishing, replacement, and repair of motors, electrical appliances, machines, and other mechanical items are taxable.

citations.title: 26 CAR §30-519(e)(1)
citations.quote: The repair or replacement of flooring is taxable.

notes: Cleaning of a building's interior or exterior is a taxable service (26 CAR §30-1003(c)(2)). Repainting is not addressed by name; it falls with nonmechanical components. The Code of Arkansas Rules is the official text from 2025-01-01, so the rule starts there; the same provisions were in the earlier Gross Receipts Tax Rules (GR series) but those versions were not read. Arkansas city and county sales taxes apply to the same sales as the state tax for this code, so this rule covers the state and local parts.

summary: Delivery charges on goods exempt from Arkansas sales tax are also exempt.

citations.title: 26 CAR §30-901(a)(2)
citations.quote: If the tangible personal property being shipped is exempt from sales and use tax, the delivery charges are also exempt from tax.

citations.title: DFA Sales and Use Tax FAQs
citations.quote: If the products being shipped are non-taxable, then the freight charges for shipping those non-taxable goods is not subject to sales and use tax.

notes: Groceries are exempt from the state tax only from 2026 (reduced before) and stay locally taxable; their delivery charge follows them, so it is locally taxable (the caller should treat the local part as delivery.taxable_goods). The Code of Arkansas Rules is the official text from 2025-01-01, so the rule starts there; the same provisions were in the earlier Gross Receipts Tax Rules (GR series) but those versions were not read.

summary: Delivery charges on taxable goods are part of the taxable gross receipts in Arkansas unless a carrier bills the buyer directly.

citations.title: 26 CAR §30-901(a)(1)
citations.quote: Delivery charges are part of the gross receipts or gross proceeds on which the tax must be collected and remitted unless the charges are billed directly to the purchaser by a carrier other than the seller.

citations.title: DFA Sales and Use Tax FAQs
citations.quote: All freight, shipping, or transportation charges are part of the gross receipts or invoice total on which sales and use tax must be collected and remitted by the seller if the products being shipped are subject to sales and use tax.

notes: With one delivery charge for taxable and exempt goods, tax applies to the share allocated to the taxable goods (26 CAR §30-901(a)(3)). The Code of Arkansas Rules is the official text from 2025-01-01, so the rule starts there; the same provisions were in the earlier Gross Receipts Tax Rules (GR series) but those versions were not read. Arkansas city and county sales taxes apply to the same sales as the state tax for this code, so this rule covers the state and local parts.

summary: Candy is taxed at the full Arkansas state sales tax rate plus local taxes: Act 141 of 2017 removed it from the reduced-rate food definition.

citations.title: DFA, What's New in Sales Tax (2017)
citations.quote: Act 141: Removes candy and soft drinks from the definitions “Food” and “Food Ingredients” and applies the full 6.5% State sales and use tax rate to these items sold at retail.

citations.title: DFA notice, Candy, Soft Drinks, and Digital Products
citations.quote: Act 141 of the 2017 Legislative Session becomes effective on January 1, 2018.

notes: Arkansas's candy definition excludes preparations containing flour and items requiring refrigeration (those are food at the reduced or, from 2026, exempt state rate). Before 2018 candy was food at the reduced state rate; not modeled. Arkansas city and county sales taxes apply to the same sales as the state tax for this code, so this rule covers the state and local parts.

summary: Custom software development and programming services are not taxable in Arkansas.

conditions.when: Sold for one unitemized price with more than a de minimis amount of software on a tangible medium, where the programming is not the true object

citations.title: 26 CAR §30-1008(h)(2)(A)
citations.quote: Software programming services and the development of custom software for a particular customer are not taxable services.

citations.title: 26 CAR §30-1008(c)(3)(B)
citations.quote: However, where there is a reasonable, separately stated charge or an invoice or other statement of the price given to the purchaser for such modification or enhancement, such modification or enhancement shall not constitute prewritten computer software.

notes: Modifications to prewritten software that are not separately charged remain part of the prewritten software (taxable only if delivered on a tangible medium). Programming sold together with software on tangible media for one price is taxable unless the programming is the true object or the media are de minimis (26 CAR §30-1008(h)(3); §30-1226). The Code of Arkansas Rules is the official text from 2025-01-01, so the rule starts there; the same provisions were in the earlier Gross Receipts Tax Rules (GR series) but those versions were not read. Arkansas city and county sales taxes apply to the same sales as the state tax for this code, so this rule covers the state and local parts.
